# System Audit — 4 March 2026

**Purpose:** Comprehensive snapshot of the entire platform as it
exists today. This document is the single source of truth for
current system state.

**Generated by:** Code agent audit, verified against live database
and codebase.

---

## 1. Database Schema

**Database:** PostgreSQL (Supabase), hosted on Hetzner via Coolify
**Tables:** 42
**RLS:** Enabled on all tables
**All PKs are `uuid` with `gen_random_uuid()` default unless noted otherwise.**

---

| Enum | Values |
|------|--------|
| `cost_formula_type` | `standard`, `ceiling_coverage`, `tiered_disposal`, `dpc_injection`, `digital_dpc`, `bag_and_cart`, `ancillary_refit`, `compound_material`, `fixed_price`, `per_room_fixed`, `skip_hire` |
| `defect_severity` | `minor`, `moderate`, `significant`, `severe`, `critical` |
| `enquiry_activity_type` | `status_change`, `assignment_change`, `note_added`, `call_logged`, `email_sent`, `survey_created`, `quotation_generated`, `quotation_sent`, `customer_notified`, `follow_up_set`, `priority_changed`, `on_hold_reason_set`, `created` |
| `enquiry_priority` | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `urgent` |
| `enquiry_status` | `new`, `assigned`, `surveyed`, `quoted`, `accepted`, `declined`, `on_hold`, `completed` |
| `item_type` | `MTL`, `LBR`, `SUB`, `OVR`, `TRA` |
| `on_hold_reason` | `awaiting_supplier`, `awaiting_customer_info`, `scheduling_conflict`, `specialist_assessment`, `customer_requested`, `other` |
| `project_status` | `draft`, `in_progress`, `pending_review`, `completed`, `archived` |
| `survey_type` | `damp`, `timber`, `woodworm`, `condensation`, `structural`, `comprehensive`, `site_preparation` |
| `uom_type` | `m2`, `lm`, `each`, `hours`, `bags`, `pairs` |
| `user_role` | `admin`, `office`, `surveyor` |

---

### Database Functions

| Function | Returns | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `get_user_role()` | `user_role` | Returns the role of the currently authenticated user from user_profiles |
| `handle_user_profiles_updated_at()` | trigger | Sets `updated_at = now()` on user_profiles row update |
| `is_admin()` | boolean | Returns true if current user has admin role |
| `is_office_or_admin()` | boolean | Returns true if current user has admin or office role |
| `set_quotation_defaults()` | trigger | Auto-generates `quotation_number` (QT-YYYY-NNNN) and computes `valid_until` on insert |
| `update_enquiry_status_changed_at()` | trigger | Sets `status_changed_at = now()` when enquiry status column changes |
| `update_updated_at()` | trigger | Generic trigger — sets `updated_at = now()` on any row update |

**Sequences:** `quotation_number_seq` — used by `set_quotation_defaults()` for sequential quotation numbering.

None.

## 2. Page Routes & Navigation

**Method:** Filesystem scan of `src/app/`, code analysis of all `page.tsx` files, and link-tracing across components. Live navigation testing was not performed (no local dev server; the app deploys to Coolify from `main`). "Works" assessments are based on code completeness and the fact that the production build succeeds.

---

### 2.1 Page Routes

| Route | File Path | Works | Reachable | Auth | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------|-----------|------|-------------|
| **Dashboard** | | | | | |
| `/` | `app/page.tsx` | Yes | Yes (sidebar) | Protected | Dashboard with stats and activity |
| **Enquiries** | | | | | |
| `/enquiries` | `app/enquiries/page.tsx` | Yes | Yes (sidebar) | Protected | Enquiry pipeline Kanban board |
| `/enquiries/new` | `app/enquiries/new/page.tsx` | Yes | Yes (from pipeline + dashboard) | Protected | New enquiry form |
| **Customers** | | | | | |
| `/customers` | `app/customers/page.tsx` | Yes | Yes (sidebar) | Protected | Customer list |
| `/customers/new` | `app/customers/new/page.tsx` | Yes | Yes (from list + dashboard + survey/new) | Protected | New customer form |

## 3. Feature-by-Feature Status

**Method:** Code reading and data-flow tracing across all source files. No data was modified. Feature status is inferred from code completeness, import resolution, and control-flow analysis.

---

### 3.1 Enquiry Pipeline

**Status:** Working
**Key files:** `src/app/enquiries/page.tsx`, `src/components/EnquiryDrawer.tsx`, `src/app/enquiries/new/page.tsx`, `src/lib/supabase-data.ts`

**What works:**

- **New enquiry form** — 3-step wizard (Client → Site → Booking) at `/enquiries/new`. Generates unique `CF-{TYPE}-{YEAR}-{NNNN}` reference number with retry on race condition. Auto-matches existing customer by email. Logs `created` activity and fires `enquiry_created` notification. Redirects to `/enquiries` on success.
- **Kanban board** — 7 columns (New, Assigned, Surveyed, Quoted, Accepted, Declined, On Hold) using `@dnd-kit/core` drag-and-drop on desktop, dropdown status change on mobile. Optimistic updates with rollback on failure. Declined and On Hold columns hidden by default with a toggle to reveal them.
- **Filtering** — text search across client name, address, postcode, and enquiry number; assignee filter; survey type filter. All client-side on loaded data.
- **Enquiry drawer** — slide-in panel with three tabs: Details (inline-editable fields for all enquiry data), Activity (timeline of `enquiry_activity` entries with Add Note and Log Call forms), Linked (associated survey, booking, quotation, and customer records).
- **Quick actions on cards** — phone shortcut (`tel:` link), email shortcut (`mailto:` link), follow-up date picker with colour-coded urgency (red = overdue, amber = today, grey = upcoming), Convert & Book button (only shown if no linked survey).
- **Convert & Book flow** — 4-step wizard embedded in the drawer (Review → Select Surveyor → Schedule via SlotPicker → Confirm). Calls `createSurveyFromEnquiry()` then `createBooking()`. Handles success, partial success (survey created but booking failed), and full failure. Auto-triggers on "Book" card button click.
- **Auto-transitions** — assigning an enquiry advances `new → assigned`; completing the survey wizard advances to `surveyed`; generating a quotation advances to `quoted`.
- **SLA indicators** — per-status time thresholds (e.g. new: 24h green / 48h amber / 48h+ red). Rendered as colour-coded dots on cards and in column headers. Drawer shows full "Time in status" and "Enquiry age" text.
- **On-hold email** — `POST /api/enquiries/[id]/notify-on-hold` sends a branded email using the reason-specific template from `on_hold_message_templates` table. Logs `customer_notified` activity. Handles missing email gracefully with a UI warning.
- **Dashboard widgets** — `PipelineWidget` shows proportional pipeline bar, active count, pipeline value, attention-needed count, and conversion %. `RecentActivityFeed` shows the 5 most recent `enquiry_activity` entries with type icons and timestamps.

**What doesn't work:**

- Missing auto-transition to `accepted` — when a customer accepts a quotation via the public page (`/api/q/[token]/respond`), the enquiry status is not advanced from `quoted` to `accepted`.
- Wizard auto-transition passes `null` as `userId` — the `surveyed` transition logs "System" as the actor rather than the surveyor who completed the wizard.

**Limitations:**

- SLA threshold constants are duplicated between `enquiries/page.tsx` and `EnquiryDrawer.tsx` with identical values — no shared constant.
- Dashboard activity feed items link to `/enquiries` (the board), not to a specific enquiry drawer.
- The enquiry form has an "Address Line 3" field with no DB column — it silently concatenates with address line 2.
- Convert & Book step 3 has a stale label ("You can change the surveyor using the selector below") but the surveyor selector is on step 2.

### 3.2 Survey System

**Status:** Working
**Key files:** `src/app/survey/new/page.tsx`, `src/app/survey/[projectId]/wizard/page.tsx`, `src/app/surveys/[surveyId]/page.tsx`, `src/app/surveys/page.tsx`

**What works:**

- **Survey creation** — form at `/survey/new` collects customer (dropdown with "Create New" redirect), survey type, site address, reported defect, scheduling notes, and optional calendar slot via `SlotPicker`. Calls `createSurveyFromForm()` to insert into `surveys` with status `draft`. If a slot is selected, also creates a `survey_bookings` row and stamps `surveyor_id` + `survey_date` on the survey. Fires `survey_created` notification.
- **Survey wizard** — 5-step room-first wizard with auto-save (2-second debounce, immediate on step navigation):
  - Step 1 (Site Details): inspection date, weather, temperature, property type, construction type, build year, street-view photo. All 5 core fields validated before proceeding.
  - Step 2 (External Inspection): building defects toggle with 17-option multi-select, wall tie and cracking concern toggles, free-text notes with audio recording and AI polish (`/api/polish-observation`), external photos.
  - Step 3 (Room Inspection): add rooms via quick-select or custom name. Per room: floor level, photo, ambient RH, multi-select issues (Damp, Condensation, Timber Decay, Woodworm), observations (typed or voice), AI polish, defect photos (up to 15), issue-specific measurement fields via `DampFields`, `CondensationFields`, `TimberFields`, `WoodwormFields` components.
  - Step 4 (Additional Works): whole-property items (PIV, ducting, airbricks, skip count, travel logistics). Fields conditionally shown based on which issue types exist across rooms.
  - Step 5 (Review): read-only summary of all collected data plus "Surveyor's Additional Comments" textarea.
- **Wizard data persistence** — `saveWizardData()` merges into `surveys.survey_data` JSONB (preserves `photos` sub-key), batch upserts `survey_rooms`, and derives `surveys.survey_tags` via `updateSurveyTags()`.
- **Survey completion** — "Complete Survey" button on step 5 sets `survey_completed = true`, `status = 'completed'`, persists tags, auto-transitions linked enquiry to `surveyed`, fires `survey_completed` notification, and redirects to the costing page.
- **Survey detail page** (`/surveys/[surveyId]`) — shows project number, type badge (from `survey_tags`), completion status, finding tags, appointment section (with inline `SlotPicker` if no booking), client details, site address, survey details, notes, quotation summary (if exists), and action buttons (Start/Continue Survey, View Costing, Generate Report, Installer Info — latter three gated on `survey_completed`).
- **Survey list** (`/surveys`) — loads all surveys with customer join, text search, status filter, type filter, grid/list view toggle. Each card/row links to `/surveys/{id}`.

**What doesn't work:**

- No validation on wizard steps 3 and 4 — surveyor can complete with zero rooms (`// TODO: Add room validation` comments in code).
- `structural` and `comprehensive` survey types are selectable in the creation dropdown but have no dedicated wizard field components, no costing sections, and no mapping logic.
- Status filter on the survey list includes `in_progress` and `pending_review` but these statuses are never set by any code — surveys go directly from `draft` to `completed`.

**Limitations:**

- No pagination on the survey list — all surveys loaded in a single query.
- Type filter uses `primarySurveyTypeFromTags()` which defaults to `damp` for surveys with no tags — selecting "Damp" also matches all untagged surveys.
- Survey list page heading still says "Projects" (legacy label).
- `createSurveyFromForm()` contains a raw `alert(JSON.stringify(error))` debug call on DB errors (line 1208 of `supabase-data.ts`).
- Surveys created via the form (not the enquiry pipeline) always have `enquiry_id = null`.

### 3.3 Costing

**Status:** Working
**Key files:** `src/app/survey/[projectId]/costing/page.tsx`, `src/lib/pricing-engine.ts`, `src/lib/survey-mapping.ts`, `src/lib/cf-csv-export.ts`

**What works:**

- **Costing page** — runs full pricing calculation on load via `generateCostingFromSurvey()`. Displays `site_preparation` results above a tabbed view per survey type (damp, condensation, timber, woodworm). Each section shows a line-item table with material and labour columns, section subtotals, adjustment % input (debounced DB write to `costing_section_adjustments`), and optional section include/exclude toggle. Sticky footer "Job Cost Summary" card shows Mandatory Works, Optional Works (included), Combined Works, PSO total, Subtotal ex-VAT, VAT (20%), Grand Total inc-VAT, and Deposit required. Deposit % reads the highest config value across active survey types from `pricing_config`.
- **Pricing engine** (`pricing-engine.ts`) — 8 formula types implemented as pure TypeScript functions: `standard`, `ceiling_coverage`, `dpc_injection`, `compound_material`, `fixed_price`, `tiered_disposal`, `bag_and_cart`, `skip_hire`. All take typed inputs and return typed outputs with no database dependencies.
- **Pricing data layer** (`pricing-data.ts`) — loads `pricing_config`, `materials_catalog`, `costing_sections` + `costing_line_templates`, and `costing_section_adjustments`. The orchestrator `calculateSurveyCosting()` loads all three dependencies in parallel, builds template lookup maps, iterates line inputs, and aggregates into `CalculationResult`.
- **Survey mapping** (`survey-mapping.ts`) — transforms `survey_data` JSONB and `survey_rooms` into `LineInput[]` per survey type. Iterates rooms, calls type-specific mappers (`mapDampRoomData`, `mapCondensationRoomData`, `mapTimberRoomData`, `mapWoodwormRoomData`), aggregates per type, and returns `Record<string, CalculationResult>`. Uses composite `"section_key:line_key"` template lookup.
- **Travel overhead** (`travel-overhead.ts`) — pure function: `CEIL(total_hours / 6.5 / num_men)` labour days × round-trip distance / 30 mph × hourly rate + vehicle mileage cost. Constants: 6.5 productive hours/day, 30 mph average, 1 vehicle. Inputs from `pricing_config` and `survey_data.additional_works`.
- **CF CSV export** (`cf-csv-export.ts` + `cf-export-config.ts`) — client-side generation of a 17-column CSV matching the Contractor Foreman upload format. Two bundle rows per CF section (Materials + Labour). Fully configured for all 4 survey types. Multi-type surveys use priority ordering `damp > timber > woodworm > condensation`. PSO handling for skip hire and travel. UTF-8 BOM for Excel compatibility. Has a test file.

**What doesn't work:**

- Some `costing_line_templates` rows have `base_unit_cost = 0` and `labour_rate_per_unit = 0` where workbooks have non-zero values (~14 timber/woodworm/condensation items) — produces £0 lines. This is a database seed issue, not a code bug.
- Three Timber treatment templates use `standard` formula but should use `ceiling_coverage` — database seed issue.
- Condensation joinery ducting template has `base_unit_cost = 0` (should be £15/m) — database seed issue.

**Limitations:**

- If `survey_data` is empty or rooms have no issues, the costing page shows "No survey data found" with no recovery path other than going back through the wizard.
- Section adjustment saves are silent (750ms debounce, no visual feedback).

### 3.4 Quotations

**Status:** Working
**Key files:** `src/app/api/surveys/[id]/quotation/route.ts`, `src/app/survey/[projectId]/quotation/[quotationId]/page.tsx`, `src/app/q/[token]/page.tsx`, `src/lib/quotation-pdf-renderer.tsx`

**What works:**

- **Quotation generation** — `POST /api/surveys/[id]/quotation` creates a frozen snapshot in `quotations` + `quotation_sections` tables. Auto-generates `quotation_number` (QT-YYYY-NNNN) and `valid_until` via database trigger. Supports versioning (increments version number per survey). Captures customer/site/surveyor/company strings, T&Cs text, and all financial totals. Auto-transitions linked enquiry to `quoted`. Fires in-app notification.
- **Internal quotation view** (`/survey/[projectId]/quotation/[quotationId]`) — two-column layout. Left: customer preview (works table grouped by type, financial summary, T&Cs, notes). Right: edit panel (validity days, notes, T&Cs textarea) with save, plus analytics panel (view count, first/last viewed, sent date). Action buttons: Copy Link, Send to Customer (admin/office only, disabled if no customer email), Download PDF.
- **Public quotation page** (`/q/[token]`) — server-rendered, no auth required, `share_token` UUID is the credential. Shows full quotation document: company header, customer/site addresses, surveyor, works table (mandatory + optional + PSO), financial summary, T&Cs, notes. Sticky action bar with PDF download and print buttons. Expiry banner shown if past `valid_until`. Response section at bottom. `noindex` robots meta.
- **Accept/decline flow** — `POST /api/q/[token]/respond`. Guards: already responded (409), expired (410), draft (403), wrong status (409). Acceptance requires signatory name, three consent checkboxes (T&Cs, cooling-off, special orders), optional cooling-off waiver. Verifies T&Cs hash hasn't changed since page load. Inserts immutable record into `quotation_acceptances` with IP, user-agent, screen resolution, consent fields, T&Cs snapshot, quotation snapshot. Updates quotation status. Fires confirmation/acknowledgement email and in-app notification.
- **View tracking** — `POST /api/q/[token]/view` inserts to `quotation_views`, increments `view_count`, sets `first_viewed_at` once, transitions `sent → viewed`, fires notification on first view. Always returns 200.
- **PDF generation** — two routes use the same `QuotationPDFDocument` renderer via `@react-pdf/renderer`: `GET /api/q/[token]/pdf` (public, no auth) and `GET /api/quotation-pdf/[quotationId]` (authenticated). A4 document with company header, addresses, works table, financial summary, T&Cs. 30-second render timeout.
- **Send to customer** — `POST /api/quotations/[id]/send`. Admin/office role required. Loads customer email, checks `isNotificationEnabled('quotation_sent', 'email')`, generates branded email with public link, sends via Resend, updates `sent_at` and transitions `draft → sent`. Fires in-app notification.

**What doesn't work:**

- Nothing identified as broken.

**Limitations:**

- Quotation generation does not check whether survey has been completed — a quotation can technically be generated from an incomplete survey if the costing page is accessed directly.

### 3.5 Reports

**Status:** Working (no PDF generation)
**Key files:** `src/lib/report-generator.ts`, `src/app/survey/[projectId]/report/page.tsx`, `src/lib/report-publish.ts`, `src/app/report/[reportId]/page.tsx`

**What works:**

- **AI report generation** — `generateReport()` in `report-generator.ts` loads survey data, wizard data, rooms, customer, surveyor, company profile, and photos. Builds per-room sub-sections filtered by issue type. Calls Grok (via OpenRouter, `x-ai/grok-4.1-fast`, temperature 0.2) only for `executive_summary` — all other sections are built programmatically from survey data. Falls back to placeholder text if LLM call fails. API route `POST /api/generate-report` requires authenticated session.
- **Report editor** (`/survey/[projectId]/report`) — auto-generates report on first open if none exists. Sections displayed as collapsible accordion cards. Inline textarea editing per section with save to `sections` JSONB (preserves `original_content`, sets `is_edited` flag). Per-section regeneration button for `executive_summary`. Status workflow toolbar: Generate → Review → Finalise → Publish/Unpublish. Photo selection panel for section-level photo attachment.
- **Publishing** — `publishReport()` generates a 64-character hex token (244 bits entropy from two `crypto.randomUUID()` values), sets `status = 'published'`, stamps `published_at`. `unpublishReport()` clears token and reverts to `finalised`. Share link displayed with copy-to-clipboard and open-in-new-tab buttons.
- **Public report page** (`/report/[reportId]?token=...`) — server-rendered, no auth, token-validated. Loads full report with customer, surveyor, company profile, and photos. Renders professional document using specialised section components (`CoverSection`, `AboutUsSection`, `RoomFindingsSection`, `ScopeOfWorksSection`, etc.). Photo lightbox via client component. `noindex` robots meta. `InvalidReportPage` fallback for invalid/missing tokens.
- **Send to customer** — `POST /api/reports/[id]/send`. Admin/office only. Requires `status === 'published'`. Loads customer email, checks notification preference, sends branded email with public link, stamps `sent_at` and `sent_to_email`, fires in-app notification.
- **View tracking** — `POST /api/report/[reportId]/view`. Public. Validates token, inserts to `report_views`, increments `view_count`, sets `first_viewed_at` once, fires in-app notification on first view.

**What doesn't work:**

- **Report PDF generation does not exist.** No `report-pdf-renderer.tsx` or `/api/report-pdf/` route exists in the codebase. CLAUDE.md incorrectly lists these as built and working. The public report page is browser-rendered HTML which can be printed to PDF manually, but there is no server-side PDF generation for reports.

**Limitations:**

- Only `executive_summary` uses LLM generation — all other report sections are data-driven templates. Re-generating a report re-runs the data assembly and the one LLM call.
- The `GET /api/report/[reportId]` JSON route exists alongside the server-rendered page — appears to be a legacy route from when the page was client-rendered. Redundant but harmless.

### 3.6 Customer Management

**Status:** Working
**Key files:** `src/app/customers/page.tsx`, `src/app/customers/new/page.tsx`, `src/app/customers/[customerId]/page.tsx`, `src/lib/customer-data.ts`

**What works:**

- **Customer list** (`/customers`) — server-side paginated (25 per page), searchable (first name, last name, email, phone, postcode with OR filter and 300ms debounce), sortable by 6 columns. Shows avatar initials, full name with title, email, phone, postcode, survey count, created date. Row click navigates to detail page.
- **Customer create** (`/customers/new`) — form with Personal Information, Contact Information, Address, and Notes sections. Client-side validation. On success: if `?returnTo=survey-new`, redirects to `/survey/new?customerId={id}`; otherwise to customer detail page.
- **Customer detail/edit** (`/customers/[customerId]`) — view mode shows all fields. Edit mode with inline form. Five cards: Customer Information (view/edit), Survey History (table with rows linking to `/surveys/[id]` + "New Survey" button), Quotations (table with rows linking to quotation detail), Bookings (table with rows linking to `/calendar`), Communications (last 10 `communication_log` entries). Danger Zone: delete button only available when survey count is 0, with confirmation modal.
- **Linking** — customer detail page queries `surveys`, `quotations`, `survey_bookings`, and `communication_log` by customer/survey relationships. Survey creation pre-populates customer via `?customerId=` URL param.

**What doesn't work:**

- **Title not saved on create** — the new customer form collects `title` (Mr/Mrs/Ms etc.) but the `createCustomer()` function in `supabase-data.ts` does not include `title` in its parameter type. The title value is dropped at line 67–79 of `customers/new/page.tsx`.
- **Title type mismatch on update** — `updateCustomer()` in `supabase-data.ts` does not include `title` in its TypeScript parameter type. The edit page passes `title` anyway (line 156 of `customers/[customerId]/page.tsx`). At runtime the spread operator (`...customerData`) forwards it to Supabase, so the update likely succeeds, but the type signature is incorrect.

**Limitations:**

- Booking rows on the customer detail page navigate to `/calendar` (the full calendar view), not to the specific booking.
- Customer creation via the enquiry pipeline's `createSurveyFromEnquiry()` has a workaround: it calls `createCustomer()` then does a separate `.update({ title })` — so title IS saved when creating customers from enquiries, but NOT when using the standalone customer form.

### 3.7 Calendar & Booking

**Status:** Working
**Key files:** `src/app/calendar/page.tsx`, `src/components/calendar/SlotPicker.tsx`, `src/lib/calendar-data.ts`, `src/app/admin/availability/page.tsx`

**What works:**

- **Calendar page** (`/calendar`) — FullCalendar React component with day/week/month/time-grid views. Per-surveyor colour coding (8-colour palette). Shows booking events (coloured by surveyor, grey for cancelled, green for completed) and absence block events (amber/striped). Surveyor filter sidebar — admin/office see all surveyors with toggle; surveyors see only their own. Event click opens inline detail panel with customer info (phone click-to-call, email click-to-email, address Google Maps link), date/time, status badge, survey link, notes. Status management dropdown (scheduled/completed/no_show) for admin/office. Cancel button for admin/office. Mobile agenda list view below 768px.
- **Booking creation** — `createBooking()` in `calendar-data.ts` inserts to `survey_bookings`. Auto-fires in-app notification to the surveyor. Called from the enquiry pipeline Convert & Book flow and the survey creation form.
- **SlotPicker** — 3-step widget: select surveyor → browse week (Mon–Sun, UK ordering) → click slot. Availability resolution from three sources in parallel: weekly hours (`surveyor_availability`), absence blocks (`availability_blocks`), existing bookings (`survey_bookings`). Interval subtraction algorithm splits remaining time into slots (default 90 minutes). Past dates shown but marked; fully-booked days show "Fully booked"; blocked days show block type icon. Empty state links to `/admin/availability` if no hours configured.
- **Booking email notifications** — `POST /api/bookings/notify` sends emails via Resend for `booking_created`, `booking_updated` (schedule changes only), and `booking_cancelled`. Branded HTML templates. Skips silently if no customer email. Logs to `communication_log`. Always returns 200. Respects `notification_preferences`.
- **Booking reminders cron** — `POST /api/cron/booking-reminders` (bearer token auth via `CRON_SECRET`). Calculates tomorrow in UK timezone (GMT/BST aware). Queries non-cancelled bookings with customer email. Deduplicates against `communication_log` to prevent double-sending. Sends reminder email to customer and creates in-app notification for surveyor. Fault-isolated per booking.
- **Surveyor availability management** (`/admin/availability`) — admin/office access. Weekly Hours section: 7-row table (Mon–Sun), toggle active days, time pickers, calculated hours, "Copy from" another surveyor. Admin can edit; office can view. Absence Blocks section: list sorted upcoming-first, add/edit modal with date range and type (annual_leave, sickness, training, other), delete with confirmation. Deep-linkable via `?surveyor=` param from team page.

**What doesn't work:**

- No booking creation directly from the calendar page — creation is only via the enquiry pipeline or survey creation form.

**Limitations:**

- Weekly hours save is a full replace (delete all + re-insert) — concurrent saves from two browser tabs would race. Acceptable for single-admin use.
- The cron job requires `CRON_SECRET` env var and an active Coolify scheduled task — whether this is wired up is not verifiable from the codebase alone.
- Booking update emails are only sent for schedule-relevant changes (date, time, surveyor) — status or notes changes do not trigger customer emails.

### 3.8 Team & Authentication

**Status:** Working
**Key files:** `src/context/AuthContext.tsx`, `src/components/ProtectedRoute.tsx`, `src/app/admin/team/page.tsx`, `src/app/api/admin/team/route.ts`

**What works:**

- **Login** (`/login`) — email + password form via `supabase.auth.signInWithPassword()`. Post-auth checks: queries `user_profiles` for `is_active` and `must_change_password`. Deactivated account → sign out + error. `must_change_password = true` → redirect to `/change-password`. No self-registration (by design).
- **Roles** — three roles (`admin`, `office`, `surveyor`) stored in `user_profiles.role`. Separate `is_surveyor` boolean flag (an admin or office user can also be a surveyor). `AuthContext` exposes `isAdmin`, `isOffice`, `isSurveyor` computed booleans. Role enforcement is per-page (client-side guard rendering "Access Restricted" screen) and per-API-route (server-side session + role check).
- **Team management** (`/admin/team`) — admin-only. Lists all `user_profiles`. Search and role filter. Add Member modal: collects display name, email, phone, role, is_surveyor flag, qualifications. `POST /api/admin/team` creates Supabase Auth user (with `email_confirm: true` to skip email verification), inserts `user_profiles` row, generates 12-character random temp password. Rolls back auth user if profile insert fails. Returns temp password for admin to share. Edit Member modal: display name, phone, role, is_surveyor, qualifications (email read-only). Self-edit: cannot change own role. Deactivate/Reactivate toggle. Self-deactivation prevented.
- **Forgot password** (`/forgot-password`) — calls `supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail()` with redirect to `/update-password`. No differentiation between found/not-found email (prevents enumeration).
- **Update password** (`/update-password`) — used after clicking email reset link. Checks for active session on mount. Password + confirm form (min 8 chars). Calls `supabase.auth.updateUser({ password })`. Does NOT clear `must_change_password` (correct — this flow is self-service reset, not forced change).
- **Change password** (`/change-password`) — forced first-login flow. Redirects away if `must_change_password` is already false. On submit: updates auth password, clears `must_change_password` on `user_profiles`, calls `refreshProfile()`, redirects to dashboard.
- **ProtectedRoute** — wraps all protected pages. Shows spinner during auth loading, redirects to `/login` if no session, redirects to `/change-password` if `mustChangePassword`. Does not check roles (that is per-page).
- **AuthContext** — two-effect initialisation pattern (avoids Supabase SDK deadlock). Effect 1: subscribes to `onAuthStateChange`. Effect 2: fetches `user_profiles` on `user.id` change. Deactivated account on session restore → auto sign-out + `profileError` message on login page. `refreshProfile()` for context refresh after password change.

**What doesn't work:**

- Nothing identified as broken.

**Limitations:**

- All route protection is client-side — no server-side middleware redirects. An unauthenticated direct URL hit loads the JS bundle before redirecting. Acceptable for an internal staff tool.
- Email cannot be changed after user creation (Supabase Auth constraint, correctly surfaced as read-only in the edit modal).

**Status:** Working

Dropdown panel shows 20 most recent notifications with type-specific icons and colour coding (17 notification types supported). Unread items highlighted with blue dot. "Mark all as read" button. Supabase Realtime subscription on `INSERT` to `notifications` table filtered to current user's profile ID — badge increments and ping animation on new notifications. Click marks as read, navigates to `link_url` or falls back to `/calendar` for booking-related notifications.

All use `sendEmail()` via Resend SDK, branded HTML templates from `email-templates.ts` reading `company_profile`, and log to `communication_log`.

Two sections: Email Configuration (platform vs custom provider mode, Resend API key, sending address, test email button) and Notification Preferences table (5 groups: Bookings, Surveys, Quotations, Reports, Enquiries & System). Per-event in-app and email toggles. Recipient type displayed as read-only badge (Internal/Customer/Both).

  - Via `calendar-data.ts`: `booking_created`, `booking_cancelled`, `booking_updated` → assigned surveyor.
- **Notification guard pattern** — every email/notification dispatch calls `isNotificationEnabled(eventType, channel)` from `notification-preferences.ts` (5-minute in-memory cache, fail-open default).

**What doesn't work:**

- Nothing identified as broken.

**Limitations:**

- `report_sent` and `report_viewed` notification types are functional in the server code but are not listed in the `NotificationBell` component's `getNotificationIcon()` or `getNotificationColors()` switch statements — they fall through to the default (plain Bell icon, no colour). Notifications are delivered but display generically.

## 4. Known Issues & Dead Code

---

### 4.1 Broken Functionality

Issues not already documented in Sections 2 or 3. Each has been verified against the current code.

| # | Issue | Location | Symptom | Severity |
|---|-------|----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | **Wizard auto-save writes stale `wizard_step`** — `handleNext()` calls `setWizardData(updatedData)` (React batched update) then immediately calls `handleAutoSave()` which reads `wizardDataRef.current`. The ref update fires in a `useEffect` that runs after the current render, so `handleAutoSave` saves the **previous** step number. | `survey/[projectId]/wizard/page.tsx:195–201` (handleNext), `:79–81` (ref sync effect), `:120` (ref read in save) | If the user navigates forward and the page reloads before any subsequent save, the wizard reopens on the wrong (previous) step. | Medium |
| 2 | **Wizard auto-save silently dropped during concurrent saves** — `handleAutoSave` is a `useCallback` with `isSaving` in its dependency array (line 145). During an active save (`isSaving = true`), any debounced save that fires will hit the `if (isSaving) return` guard and silently discard the data. Because `isSaving` is a closure value (not a ref), the recreated callback also cascades to `triggerDebouncedSave`, which can cancel pending timers. | `survey/[projectId]/wizard/page.tsx:112–145` (handleAutoSave), `:148–156` (triggerDebouncedSave) | If a user edits data while a save is in progress and the save takes longer than the 2-second debounce, the edit is silently lost until the next user interaction triggers another save cycle. | Medium |
| 3 | **CF CSV export uses hardcoded hourly rate** — `STANDARD_HOURLY_RATE = 30.63` is a constant at line 46. The admin can change `hourly_labour_rate` via `/admin/rates`, but the CSV export does not read from `pricing_config`. The pricing engine and travel overhead calculator both correctly read the rate from the database. | `lib/cf-csv-export.ts:46` | If the admin changes the hourly rate, the Contractor Foreman CSV export will calculate pre-markup labour costs using the stale hardcoded rate, producing incorrect values. All other calculations use the correct rate. | Medium |
| 4 | **EnquiryDrawer inline edits fail silently** — 8 `catch` blocks in the drawer's action handlers log to `console.error` but show no UI feedback. The user performs an action (change status, change priority, assign, save notes, set value, set follow-up date, add note, log call), it fails, and the UI shows no error — the optimistic update just quietly reverts (or doesn't revert at all if `onBoardSync` was called before the error). | `components/EnquiryDrawer.tsx:870–874` (status), `:897–900` (priority), `:924–927` (assignment), `:937–940` (notes), `:951–954` (value), `:1012–1015` (follow-up), `:1040–1043` (add note), `:1069–1072` (log call) | User edits enquiry data, the save fails (network error, RLS denial), no error message appears. The change appears to succeed but is lost on page reload. | High |
| 5 | **EnquiryDrawer `saveField` has zero error handling** — the inline field editor (`saveField` callback, lines 963–993) calls `updateEnquiry()` and raw Supabase `.update()` with no try/catch wrapper. If either throws, it becomes an unhandled promise rejection. | `components/EnquiryDrawer.tsx:963–993` | Editing inline fields (client name, email, phone, source, survey date, reported problem, site address fields) can throw an unhandled error to the console with no user-visible feedback. | High |
| 6 | **Costing page section saves are fire-and-forget with no error handling** — `saveSectionAdjustment()` is called inside a `setTimeout` callback (line 387) with no try/catch or `.catch()`. `saveSectionInclusion()` is similarly unguarded (line 394). Section 3.3 notes these are "silent" but the specific issue is that errors are completely unhandled. | `survey/[projectId]/costing/page.tsx:387` (adjustment), `:394` (inclusion) | If saving a section adjustment or inclusion toggle fails (network, RLS), the error is swallowed. The UI shows the changed value but it's lost on page reload. | Medium |
| 7 | **`report-generator.ts` crashes on missing company profile** — `profile!` non-null assertion used on lines 1033–1034 and 2025–2026. `profile` is typed `CompanyProfile | null`. If the `company_profile` table has no row (first-time setup), `buildGuaranteeParagraph(profile!)` throws `Cannot read properties of null`. | `lib/report-generator.ts:1033–1034, 2025–2026` | Generating or regenerating a report crashes with an unhandled null reference error if the company profile has not been configured. | Medium |
| 8 | **AuthContext has no profile fetch timeout** — `fetchProfile()` in AuthContext.tsx (lines 34–56) is a plain `await supabase.from().select().single()` with no `AbortController`, no `setTimeout`, and no fallback. | `context/AuthContext.tsx:34–56` | If the Supabase connection hangs (network outage, DNS failure), `isLoading` stays `true` indefinitely and the entire app is stuck on a loading spinner with no recovery path. | Medium |
| 9 | **`supabase-client.ts` returns `null` disguised as a typed Supabase client** — when environment variables are missing, `createClient()` returns `null as unknown as ReturnType<typeof createBrowserClient>` (line 16). TypeScript cannot catch subsequent calls to `supabase.from(...)` which will throw `Cannot read properties of null`. | `lib/supabase-client.ts:16` | If `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` or `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are missing, every Supabase call in the app throws an opaque null reference error. The double type cast makes this invisible to TypeScript. | Low |

### 4.6 Console Errors & Warnings

#### 4.6.1 AuthContext Profile Fetch — No Timeout

`fetchProfile()` in `AuthContext.tsx` (lines 34–56) uses a plain `await supabase.from('user_profiles').select('*')...single()` with no `AbortController`, no `setTimeout`, and no fallback timer. If the Supabase connection hangs, `isLoading` stays `true` forever and the app is stuck on a loading spinner. The `cancelled` flag (line 93) only guards against stale React updates after component unmount — it does not abort the HTTP request.

#### 4.6.2 `middleware.ts` — Exists But Does Not Handle Route Protection

`src/middleware.ts` exists (confirmed), but its sole job is JWT token refresh. Line 39 comments explicitly: *"Route protection is intentionally NOT handled here — ProtectedRoute (client-side) handles that without needing a middleware refactor."* All auth redirects are client-side only. A user navigating directly to a protected URL will briefly see the page shell/loading state before the client-side redirect fires.

## 5. Technical Debt

Things that work but are implemented in ways that will cause problems as the system grows, or that deviate from best practices. Each item documents what the debt is, where it lives, and why it matters. Items are not prioritised here — that is for the planning document.

---

### 5.1 Architecture & Patterns

#### 5.1.1 `middleware.ts` — JWT Refresh Only, No Route Protection

- **What:** `src/middleware.ts` creates a Supabase SSR client on every request and calls `supabase.auth.getUser()` to trigger JWT validation and cookie refresh. It always returns `NextResponse.next()` regardless of session state. Line 38–39 comments explicitly: *"Route protection is intentionally NOT handled here — ProtectedRoute (client-side) handles that without needing a middleware refactor."*
- **Where:** `src/middleware.ts`
- **Why it matters:** An unauthenticated user who navigates directly to any protected URL (e.g. `/surveys`, `/admin/rates`) receives the full page HTML before the client-side `ProtectedRoute` component hydrates and redirects. For an internal staff tool this is low practical risk, but it means protected page markup is served to unauthenticated requests.

#### 5.1.2 No `loading.tsx` at Any Route Level

- **What:** There is no `loading.tsx` file anywhere in `src/app/` — not at the root level and not in any route segment. A root-level `error.tsx` and `not-found.tsx` exist, but no nested `error.tsx` or `not-found.tsx` exist in any sub-route.
- **Where:** Absent from all 30+ route directories under `src/app/`.
- **Why it matters:** Next.js has no Suspense boundary to show a streaming skeleton while any page loads — the user sees a blank or frozen viewport until client-side data fetching completes and state is set. Each of the 22+ authenticated pages implements its own loading spinner via `useState` boolean flags, resulting in 22+ independent loading-state implementations with no shared pattern.

#### 5.1.3 No Nested `error.tsx` Boundaries

- **What:** The single root-level `error.tsx` is the only error boundary in the app. No route segment has its own `error.tsx`.
- **Where:** Only `src/app/error.tsx` exists.
- **Why it matters:** A JavaScript error inside any page (e.g. `/admin/rates`, `/survey/[projectId]/costing`) bubbles all the way to the root boundary. The root error page offers no route-specific context or recovery path — the user must navigate away from the entire section.

#### 5.1.4 Every Authenticated Page Is a Client Component

- **What:** All 28 authenticated `page.tsx` files are `'use client'` components. Not one is a React Server Component. Data is fetched exclusively client-side via `useEffect` + `useState` patterns calling the browser Supabase client. The only Server Components are the two public pages (`/q/[token]/page.tsx` and `/report/[reportId]/page.tsx`), which use `createServerClient` with the service-role key.
- **Where:** Every `page.tsx` under `src/app/` except the two public pages.
- **Why it matters:** The internal app never benefits from server-side rendering, streaming, or Next.js caching for authenticated data. Every page load requires a full client-side hydration cycle, a Supabase auth check, and then data fetching — all sequential. This is the root cause of the flash-of-loading-spinner on every navigation.

#### 5.1.5 Four Distinct Service-Role Client Construction Patterns

- **What:** API routes that need a service-role Supabase client construct one in four different ways:
  1. `createClient` from `@supabase/supabase-js` — used by 9 routes (quotation, report send, booking notify, cron, etc.).
  2. `createServerClient` from `@supabase/ssr` with no-op cookie handlers — used by 2 routes (`/api/report/[reportId]`, `/api/settings/notifications`).
  3. Inline `createServerClient` with ad-hoc `cookies()` construction — used by `/api/quotation-pdf/[quotationId]`.
  4. Module-level singleton caching (`_adminClient` / `_client`) — used by `notifications-server.ts` and `notification-preferences.ts`.
- **Where:** 9+ API route files and 2 lib files.
- **Why it matters:** No shared factory function exists for the service-role client. The construction logic is duplicated across at least 9 routes, and subtle differences (cookie handling, SSR library vs plain library) make it unclear which pattern is correct for new routes.

#### 5.1.6 `update-password/page.tsx` Uses `getSession()` Instead of `getUser()`

- **What:** `src/app/update-password/page.tsx` (line 21) calls `supabase.auth.getSession()` to check if a user is logged in. Every other auth check in the app uses `supabase.auth.getUser()`.
- **Where:** `src/app/update-password/page.tsx:21`
- **Why it matters:** `getSession()` reads from local storage without re-validating the JWT against Supabase servers, making it a weaker check. A stale or forged local session would pass `getSession()` but fail `getUser()`. This is the only page using the weaker check.

---

### 5.2 Data Model

#### 5.2.1 Two Pairs of Duplicate Progress/Completion Columns on `surveys`

- **What:** The `surveys` table has four columns representing two concepts:

  | Concept | Column A (used) | Column B (unused) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Completion percentage | `survey_progress` | `completion_pct` |
  | Completion flag | `survey_completed` | `is_complete` |

  All live code reads/writes the `survey_progress` / `survey_completed` pair. `completion_pct` and `is_complete` are declared in the TypeScript type (`database.types.ts`, lines 167–168) but are never read or written by any code path. Both pairs have their own database indexes.
- **Where:** `00000000000000_initial_schema.sql` (lines 222–233); `src/types/database.types.ts` (lines 167–168).
- **Why it matters:** Any future code that picks the wrong column will silently produce stale data — both unused columns default to `0`/`false`, making the mismatch invisible without a deliberate cross-check. The orphan indexes also consume storage and write overhead.

#### 5.2.2 Never-Populated Columns on `surveys`

Three columns exist in the schema and TypeScript types but are never written to by any code path:

| Column | Schema location | Code status |
|---|---|---|
| `office_notes TEXT` | `initial_schema.sql:236` | Zero reads or writes anywhere. A separate `notes` column is used instead. |
| `submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ` | `initial_schema.sql:235` | Zero writes. Declared in `database.types.ts:169` only. |
| `reported_problem_override TEXT` | `initial_schema.sql:231` | Read once (`surveys/[surveyId]/page.tsx:289`: `survey.reported_problem_override \|\| survey.reported_problem`) but never written. The override always evaluates to null, and the fallback always wins. |

- **Why it matters:** Each consumes TypeScript surface area and schema space without contributing data. `reported_problem_override` introduces a dead branch in the survey detail page.

#### 5.2.3 `survey_type` Ghost Enum Values

- **What:** The `survey_type` enum includes `structural`, `comprehensive` (from `initial_schema.sql`, lines 60–67), and `site_preparation` (from `20260301000002_add_site_preparation_survey_type.sql`). None of these three have wizard steps, mapping engine logic, or report templates.
- **Where:** The new survey form (`src/app/survey/new/page.tsx`, lines 28–35) exposes `structural` and `comprehensive` as selectable options. `site_preparation` exists in the enum and as costing sections but has no UI path to create one.
- **Why it matters:** A user selecting `structural` or `comprehensive` creates a survey that the wizard, mapping engine, and report generator cannot process — a silent dead-end. `site_preparation` has costing data but no creation UI.

#### 5.2.4 Stale Column Comment on `surveys.surveyor_id`

- **What:** The FK migration (`20260302000001_surveyor_identity_migration.sql`, lines 50–58) correctly re-pointed `surveys.surveyor_id` from the deleted `surveyors` table to `user_profiles(id)`. However, the column comment in `initial_schema.sql` still reads *"Reference to the assigned surveyor from the surveyors table"*. The `surveyors` table no longer exists.
- **Where:** `00000000000000_initial_schema.sql:785` (comment); `20260302000001_surveyor_identity_migration.sql:50–58` (correct FK).
- **Why it matters:** Documentation-only inconsistency — the live FK is correct, but anyone reading the schema file will believe `surveyor_id` still references the deleted table.

#### 5.2.5 `enquiries.source` — Free-Text Column With Inconsistent UI Casing

- **What:** The `source` column on `enquiries` is `TEXT` with no database constraint. Two different UIs write to it with different casing:
  - Enquiry creation form (`src/app/enquiries/new/page.tsx`, lines 285–292): stores **lowercase** — `website`, `phone`, `email`, `referral`, `repeat`.
  - EnquiryDrawer edit (`src/components/EnquiryDrawer.tsx`, lines 115–122): stores **Title Case** — `Website`, `Phone`, `Email`, `Referral`, `Repeat Customer`.
  - The creation form uses `"repeat"`; the drawer uses `"Repeat Customer"` — a label mismatch beyond just casing.
- **Where:** `src/app/enquiries/new/page.tsx:285–292` and `src/components/EnquiryDrawer.tsx:115–122`.
- **Why it matters:** Filtering, grouping, or reporting on `source` will treat `website` and `Website` as different values, silently splitting the same lead source into two buckets with no database-level protection.

#### 5.3.4 Type Safety Gaps

**`as any` — 36 usages across 9 files:**

| File | Count | Root cause |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/report-generator.ts` | 20 | JSONB `room_data` cast at point of access (`room.room_data?.damp as any`, `sd as any`, etc.) |
| `src/lib/survey-tags.ts` | 4 | Same: untyped JSONB `room_data` |
| `src/lib/report-data.ts` | 3 | Report `sections` JSONB cast when reading from DB |
| `src/components/wizard/AdditionalWorksStep.tsx` | 3 | Form value type mismatches |
| `src/lib/survey-wizard-data.ts` | 2 | JSONB `room_data` |
| `src/lib/survey-photo-service.ts` | 1 | Storage folder name |
| `src/lib/survey-mapping.ts` | 1 | Supabase join result |
| `src/components/wizard/RoomInspectionStep.tsx` | 1 | Floor level assignment |
| `src/app/surveys/[surveyId]/page.tsx` | 1 | `survey_data` JSONB access |

28 of 36 `as any` usages stem from one root cause: `survey_rooms.room_data` and `surveys.survey_data` are stored as JSONB in Postgres and returned as untyped objects. Every consumer casts to `any` at point of use rather than going through a single typed accessor. The typed wizard types exist in `survey-wizard.types.ts` but are not applied when reading back from the database.

**`: any` type annotations — 36 usages across 15 files:**

| File | Count | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/report-generator.ts` | 16 | Function parameters (`condensationRooms: any[]`, `sd: any`, `aw: any`) and local variables |
| `src/lib/pricing-data.ts` | 3 | Supabase query result mappings (`.map((section: any)`) |
| `src/app/api/report/[reportId]/route.ts` | 3 | `surveyData: any`, `allPhotos: any[]` |
| `src/app/admin/team/page.tsx` | 3 | `catch (err: any)` pattern |
| Wizard field components (×8) | 1 each | `handleChange(field, value: any)` repeated across `SiteDetailsStep`, `AdditionalWorksStep`, `CondensationFields`, `ExternalInspectionStep`, `WoodwormFields`, `RoomInspectionStep`, `TimberFields`, `DampFields` |

The `handleChange(field, value: any)` pattern across all 8 wizard field components is the second most common structural type-unsafety in the codebase — each component defines its own `handleChange` with an `any` value parameter to avoid a union type.

### 5.4 Security

#### 5.4.1 API Routes With Authentication But No Role Check

Seven API routes verify that the caller is authenticated but do not check their role, allowing any authenticated user (including surveyors) to invoke them:

| Route | File | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/generate-report` | `src/app/api/generate-report/route.ts:34–38` | Triggers a paid LLM call (OpenRouter) for any `surveyId`. Any authenticated user can generate AI content for surveys they have no relation to, at the company's API cost. |
| `POST /api/transcribe` | `src/app/api/transcribe/route.ts:36–39` | Forwards arbitrary audio to the paid Deepgram API. No throttling or ownership check. |
| `POST /api/polish-observation` | `src/app/api/polish-observation/route.ts:21–24` | Sends arbitrary text to OpenRouter LLM at the company's expense. |
| `POST /api/surveys/[id]/quotation` | `src/app/api/surveys/[id]/quotation/route.ts:28–37` | Creates a quotation (financial document) and advances the linked enquiry to `quoted` status. Any surveyor can generate quotations for any survey. |
| `GET & PATCH /api/settings/company` | `src/app/api/settings/company/route.ts:42–51, 84–91` | Any authenticated user can read and overwrite company identity fields including `terms_and_conditions`, `vat_number`, and `company_registration_number`. Line 79 comments: *"restrict to admin later if needed."* |
| `POST /api/settings/company/logo` | `src/app/api/settings/company/logo/route.ts:15–23` | Any authenticated user can upload a new company logo, replacing the existing one. |
| `POST /api/notifications/trigger` | `src/app/api/notifications/trigger/route.ts:101–105` | Any authenticated user can fire system notifications with arbitrary entity IDs and event types, causing false alerts in the notification feed. |

#### 5.4.2 Hardcoded Secrets in Source Code

No hardcoded API keys, passwords, or credentials were found in any `.ts` or `.tsx` file under `src/`. All service credentials are correctly read from `process.env`.

#### 5.4.3 RLS Gaps

**A. Broad "Authenticated Users Full Access" on High-Value Tables**

Migration `00000000000000_initial_schema.sql` (lines 887–900) grants full SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE to every `authenticated` user on the following tables, regardless of role:

`customers`, `enquiries`, `surveys`, `survey_rooms`, `photos`, `moisture_readings`, `materials_catalog`, `pricing_items`, `project_costing`, `work_sections`, `defects`, `markup_config`, `base_rates`.

Any surveyor can delete any customer record, survey, photo, or enquiry directly via the Supabase client at the database level. Application-level role checks in API routes are the only barrier — they do not cover direct database access.

**B. Costing Configuration Tables Writable by All Authenticated Users**

Migration `00000000000000_initial_schema.sql` (lines 926–951): `costing_sections`, `costing_line_templates`, `costing_section_adjustments`, and `pricing_config` all have INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE policies open to any `authenticated` user. Any surveyor can alter hourly labour rates, material costs, or delete costing templates directly, bypassing the admin-only `/admin/rates` UI.

**C. `report_templates` — Any Authenticated User Can Delete**

Migration `00000000000000_initial_schema.sql` (line 957): `DELETE` policy on `report_templates` is open to all `authenticated` users. Any surveyor can delete the seeded default report templates.

**D. `quotations` Anonymous SELECT Is Unrestricted at RLS Level**

Migration `20260301000004_quotation_schema.sql` (lines 192–193): the `anon` SELECT policy on `quotations` uses `USING (true)` with no filter on `share_token`. The comment states the UUID share_token is the access credential and the app always filters by it — but RLS does not enforce this. An anonymous caller who obtains any valid `quotation.id` UUID can fetch that row without the share token. The same pattern applies to `quotation_sections`.

**E. `quotation_acceptances` SELECT Policy Has Broken Join**

Migration `20260302000010_quotation_acceptances.sql` (lines 62–71): the admin/office SELECT policy joins `user_profiles.id = auth.uid()`, but `user_profiles.id` is the profile UUID while `auth.uid()` returns the auth user UUID (which maps to `user_profiles.user_id`, not `user_profiles.id`). The `EXISTS` subquery never matches any row, so no authenticated user — including admins — can read `quotation_acceptances` via RLS. All reads go through the service-role client which bypasses RLS, masking the bug.

**F. `company_profile` — Any Authenticated User Can UPDATE**

Migration `20260301000006_company_profile.sql` (lines 78–84): the UPDATE policy has `USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)` for all `authenticated` users. Any surveyor can overwrite the company's legal identity fields directly at the database level. The comment in the migration reads: *"restrict to admin later if needed."*

---

### 5.5 Performance

#### 5.5.1 Unbounded Full-Table Fetches

Several core data-fetching functions return the entire table contents with no `.limit()`:

| Function | File | What it fetches |
|---|---|---|
| `getSurveys()` | `src/lib/supabase-data.ts:1073` | All surveys including full `survey_data` JSONB + joined customer. No limit. |
| `getEnquiries()` | `src/lib/supabase-data.ts:381` | All enquiries, `select('*')`, no limit. |
| `getEnquiriesByStatus()` | `src/lib/supabase-data.ts:927` | All enquiries + two joins (user_profiles, customers), no limit. Grouped in JavaScript on the client. |
| `getCustomers()` | `src/lib/supabase-data.ts:76` | All customers, `select('*')`, no limit. |

As the volume of surveys, enquiries, and customers grows, these queries will return unbounded result sets to the browser. The `survey_data` JSONB column alone can be kilobytes per row.

#### 5.5.2 Dashboard Fetches All Surveys to Display 5 Rows

- **Where:** `src/app/page.tsx:115–119`
- **What:** `getSurveys()` returns the full surveys table. The dashboard uses `surveys.slice(0, 5)` for the "Recent Projects" panel and `.filter()` for the 4 stat cards (`active`, `pending`, `draft`, `total`). Every byte of every survey's `survey_data` JSONB is transferred to the browser to compute 4 integers and display 5 rows. These are aggregations that Postgres could compute without transferring any data rows.

#### 5.5.3 Read-Before-Write Patterns

Several functions perform a read round-trip before every write where a single upsert or direct write would suffice:

| Function | File | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `saveReport()` | `src/lib/report-data.ts:25–66` | Reads `select('id')` to check existence, then issues either an update or insert — two round-trips per save. |
| `updateReportSection()` | `src/lib/report-data.ts:175–205` | Calls `loadReport()` (`select('*')`) to get all sections, mutates one section in JavaScript, writes the entire sections array back. Full read on every keystroke save. |
| `saveWizardData()` | `src/lib/survey-wizard-data.ts:122–148` | Reads `select('survey_data')` before every auto-save to merge with existing data, then writes back — 2 DB calls per auto-save cycle. |
| `saveSectionAdjustment()` | `src/lib/pricing-data.ts:390–413` | Queries `costing_sections` by `section_key` + `survey_type` to find the UUID before upserting. Every slider movement fires two DB queries. |
| `saveSectionInclusion()` | `src/lib/pricing-data.ts:437–461` | Same pattern as `saveSectionAdjustment()`. |

#### 5.5.4 Sequential Queries That Could Be Parallelised

| Location | File | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `generateReport()` | `src/lib/report-generator.ts:662–721` | Five sequential queries: survey → company profile → wizardData (2 internal queries) → customer → surveyor. Customer and surveyor fetches could run concurrently. |
| `getCustomerDetail()` | `src/lib/customer-data.ts:167–271` | Five sequential queries: customer → surveys → quotations → bookings → communications. Quotations and bookings could be parallelised after surveys resolves. |
| Costing page load | `src/app/survey/[projectId]/costing/page.tsx:299–378` | Calls `loadPricingConfig()` twice — once inside `calculateSurveyCosting()` and once directly. Also loads wizard data, section adjustments, inclusions, and optional flags in a mixed sequential/parallel pattern. |

#### 5.5.5 Missing Database Indexes

| Column(s) | Table | Used by | Why missing matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| `survey_tags` (TEXT[]) | `surveys` | Tag filtering | No GIN index for array-containment queries. Added in migration `20260302000001_add_survey_tags.sql` with no accompanying index. |
| `client_name`, `client_phone`, `enquiry_number` | `enquiries` | `ilike` search in `getEnquiryList()` (`supabase-data.ts:424–429`) | No trigram (`pg_trgm`) GIN index. `%term%` patterns on these columns force sequential scans. Only `status` and `created_at` B-tree indexes exist. |
| `first_name`, `phone` | `customers` | `ilike` search in `getCustomerList()` (`customer-data.ts:102–106`) | Existing indexes cover `email`, `(last_name, first_name)`, and `postcode` — but `%term%` patterns on `first_name` or `phone` alone still require sequential scans. |
| `status` | `survey_bookings` | `.neq('status', 'cancelled')` in `getAvailableSlots()` (`calendar-data.ts:776`) | Indexes exist on `surveyor_id`, `booking_date`, and `survey_id` but not `status`. |
| `(enquiry_id, created_at DESC)` composite | `enquiry_activity` | `getEnquiryActivities()` filters by `enquiry_id` and orders by `created_at DESC` | Separate indexes on each column exist, but a composite would serve both predicates in one seek. |

#### 5.5.6 Client-Side Filtering of Full Datasets

| Page | File | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Surveys list | `src/app/surveys/page.tsx:48–72` | Fetches all surveys including full `survey_data` JSONB via `getSurveys()`. All search, status, and type filtering happens in the browser via `surveys.filter()`. Only 7 columns are displayed; the full JSONB is transferred but never read. |
| Enquiries board | `src/app/enquiries/page.tsx:1221–1300` | Fetches all enquiries plus a second query for related `surveys`. Client-side `filteredBoard` memo operates on the full dataset. |
| Customer list survey counts | `src/lib/customer-data.ts:141–153` | After fetching paginated customers, a second query fetches `select('customer_id')` from `surveys` — one row per survey, not an aggregate count. Counts are accumulated in a JavaScript loop. `COUNT(*) GROUP BY customer_id` would avoid transferring individual rows. |

#### 5.5.7 Component Re-render Patterns

- **Wizard page** (`src/app/survey/[projectId]/wizard/page.tsx:52–82`): The entire `wizardData` (deeply nested JSONB object) and `rooms` array are held as flat top-level `useState`. Any change to a single field in any room replaces the entire `rooms` array, causing every child component to re-evaluate. No `useMemo` or `React.memo` is applied to step components.
- **Enquiry pipeline board** (`src/app/enquiries/page.tsx`, ~lines 1389–1430): The `board` state is a `Record<string, Enquiry[]>` containing all enquiries across all columns. Any drag-and-drop or status update creates a new `board` object, triggering `filteredBoard` recomputation and re-render of all 7 `KanbanColumn` components and every `EnquiryCard`.
- **NotificationBell** (`src/components/NotificationBell.tsx:130–133`): Runs a `select('*', {count: 'exact', head: true})` on every mount. Since the bell is inside the Layout component, it fires a fresh database query on every page navigation, in addition to setting up a Realtime subscription on every mount.
- **`saveAllRooms()`** (`src/lib/survey-wizard-data.ts:353–354`): Saves rooms sequentially in a `for` loop with `await` per iteration — one database round-trip per room. A survey with 6 rooms generates 6 serial round-trips on every auto-save.

**Next.js Configuration (`next.config.mjs`):**
- `output: 'standalone'` — produces a self-contained server for Docker
- `images.domains` — allows images from localhost and the Supabase URL
- `experimental.serverActions.bodySizeLimit: '10mb'` — supports large photo uploads via server actions
- `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true` — the build succeeds even with type errors

### 6.3 Environment Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Where Used |
|---|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | Supabase project URL (public, embedded in client bundle) | `supabase-client.ts`, `supabase-server.ts`, `middleware.ts`, all API routes using service client, `next.config.mjs` image domains |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | Supabase anonymous/public key (public, embedded in client bundle) | `supabase-client.ts`, `supabase-server.ts`, `middleware.ts`, `quotation-pdf` route |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | Supabase service-role key (server-only, bypasses RLS) | 15+ API routes, `email-config.ts`, `email-service.ts`, `email-templates.ts`, `notifications-server.ts`, `notification-preferences.ts`, `company-profile.ts`, public pages (`/q/[token]`, `/report/[reportId]`) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | Public-facing app URL (used in email links, quotation links) | `email-templates.ts`, `report-publish.ts`, quotation/report send routes |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` | Alternative site URL (used in LLM HTTP-Referer headers) | `report-generator.ts`, `generate-report` route, `polish-observation` route |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | OpenRouter API key for LLM calls (server-only) | `api/generate-report/route.ts`, `api/polish-observation/route.ts` |
| `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` | Deepgram API key for speech-to-text (server-only) | `api/transcribe/route.ts` |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | Resend email API key (server-only, fallback if not in platform_settings) | `email-config.ts` — used as fallback when `platform_resend_api_key` is not set in `platform_settings` table |
| `CRON_SECRET` | Shared secret for authenticated cron endpoints | `cron-auth.ts` — validates `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` header on cron routes |
| `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` | Disables Next.js telemetry (set to `1` in Dockerfile) | Dockerfile build and run stages |
| `NODE_ENV` | Runtime environment (`production` in Dockerfile) | Dockerfile runner stage |
| `PORT` | HTTP listen port (`3000` in Dockerfile) | Dockerfile runner stage |
| `HOSTNAME` | Bind address (`0.0.0.0` in Dockerfile) | Dockerfile runner stage |

**Notes:**
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` serve overlapping purposes (both provide the app's public URL). `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` is used for user-facing links in emails; `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` is used for LLM HTTP-Referer headers. Both fall back to `http://localhost:3000`.
- `.env.example` lists: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, `CRON_SECRET`.
- `.env.local.example` lists: `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
- Neither template file lists `RESEND_API_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` (only in `.env.example`), or `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` (in no template).

### 6.4 Dockerfile

**File:** `survey-system/Dockerfile` (35 lines)

**Architecture:** Two-stage build (builder → runner)

| Stage | Base Image | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `builder` | `node:22-alpine` | Install deps (`npm ci`), copy source, run `npm run build` |
| `runner` | `node:22-alpine` | Production runtime — minimal image with standalone output only |

**Build stage:**
1. Copies `package.json` + `package-lock.json` → runs `npm ci`
2. Copies full source tree
3. Sets `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`
4. Runs `npm run build` (produces `.next/standalone/` via Next.js standalone output)

**Runner stage:**
1. Sets `NODE_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0`
2. Creates non-root user `nextjs` (uid 1001, group `nodejs`)
3. Copies three artefacts from builder:
   - `public/` → `./public` (static assets — **must exist or build fails**, see note below)
   - `.next/standalone/` → `./` (Node.js server + dependencies)
   - `.next/static/` → `./.next/static/` (hashed client bundles)
4. Runs as non-root user `nextjs`
5. Exposes port 3000
6. Entrypoint: `node server.js`

**Critical requirement:** Line 27 (`COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public`) requires the `public/` directory to exist in the Git repository. Git does not track empty directories. If all files in `public/` are deleted, the directory vanishes from Git and the Docker build fails silently on Coolify. A `.gitkeep` file must be maintained in `public/` at all times (see Memory: Docker Build — Critical Dependencies).

**Not present:**
- No health check (`HEALTHCHECK` instruction)
- No multi-platform build configuration
- No `.dockerignore` file (the full source tree is copied into the builder stage)

**Also present:** `docker-compose.yml` — defines a local PostgreSQL 15 + Adminer setup for local development, but is **not used** in the current workflow (all development and testing happens against the remote Supabase instance on Hetzner).
